title: Workspace Lambda Multi-Repository Research Execution v1
goal: Generalize the accepted GitHub-to-Lambda execution substrate from a research-engine-specific pilot into a reusable, fail-closed, manifest-driven research compute control plane that can execute bounded candidate code from research-engine, PADataset, and future explicitly authorized research repositories without per-task controller/provisioner/runtime patches or routine human SSH/sudo intervention.
acceptance_criteria: The accepted one-job JIT execution model, root/unprivileged privilege split, exact candidate/workflow attestation, resource bounding, private/local-network denial, trusted-cache immutability, durable receipts, cleanup, and quarantine semantics remain intact.

Controller configuration is project-parameterized: repository, project_id, scale-set names, runner namespaces, and project-specific workflow claims are derived from root-owned/project configuration rather than fixed research-engine constants.

The root provisioner resolves project_id through an explicit root-owned project registry and validates the corresponding manifest; it no longer defaults operational authority to one research-engine manifest or one research-engine runner-name regex.

Privileged runtime authorization is semantic/capability-driven. Exact workload names such as model-eval-dual-gpu or model-eval-local-extract-wave1 are not used as privileged authorization gates; root-owned manifest/policy resource class, execution profile, model/runtime binding, egress, secrets, state-effect, and cache declarations determine allowed behavior.

Generic workload families are reusable across experiments. A new benchmark/task using an already-authorized CPU/GPU/model envelope does not require adding a new workload string to controller, provisioner service, or runtime.
Each authorized repository receives a distinct project identity and isolated writable roots/logs/staging/cache namespace, with cross-project read/write denial proven for project-owned mutable state.

Shared promoted runtime/model objects may be referenced read-only across projects only when the root policy explicitly authorizes that object for each project; target repositories cannot promote or mutate shared trusted objects.

Project onboarding is declarative and Git-driven. After the generalization is installed, adding an explicitly approved repository/project manifest and trusted launcher through workspace-control can reconcile the required project identity, directories, controller instances/scale sets, and policy without routine operator SSH/sudo.

Target-repository candidate code cannot onboard itself, alter root project policy, mint new execution profiles, widen network/secrets/filesystem authority, or cause arbitrary repositories to be accepted.
PADataset is the first second-project pilot. After genericization, onboarding PADataset requires only project manifest/workflow/config additions and no controller/provisioner/runtime source changes.
PADataset proves at least one CPU execution and one GPU execution through fresh ephemeral runners, with exact candidate SHA binding, durable receipts, cleanup, and zero residue/quarantine.

Cross-project isolation is adversarially demonstrated: PADataset candidate code cannot read/write research-engine mutable roots, credentials, JIT material, or project-private caches, and research-engine retains the reciprocal boundary.
Existing research-engine CPU/GPU/model-eval routes continue to pass regression unchanged after generalization.

A third future repository can be represented by schema/contract tests using only a new manifest/route fixture, demonstrating that source-code changes are not structurally required for repository expansion.
constraints: Do not weaken the accepted fail-closed security boundary merely to make onboarding easier.
Do not replace project isolation with one broadly writable shared research UID unless equivalent or stronger filesystem/process/cache isolation is proven first.

Do not grant candidate jobs root, sudo, Docker socket, SSH keys, personal home access, controller credentials, GitHub controller tokens, production database credentials, or arbitrary local/private-network access.
Do not make the root provisioner depend on target-repository-controlled policy files. Root authority must remain in workspace-control/root-owned installed configuration.
Do not allow arbitrary GitHub repositories or arbitrary owners; every project remains explicitly allowlisted by exact repository identity.
Do not let target candidate code trigger project onboarding/reconciliation or trusted-cache promotion.
Preserve exact one-job ephemeral runner cleanup and receipt semantics.
Preserve generic gpu-heavy DENY except where a root-owned project route maps a trusted workflow to an accepted heavy resource class.
Do not modify research-engine production routing or scientific state while generalizing the execution substrate.
PADataset pilot changes should be control-plane/workflow/canary only until the generic substrate is accepted; do not alter PADataset scientific results or paper claims merely to prove execution.
Routine future candidate-code execution and approved-project onboarding should not require manual operator terminal intervention after this task's final root-control-plane activation.

Any unavoidable one-time root installation required to activate the generic control-plane implementation must be explicit, bounded, and the last routine sudo dependency for subsequent approved-project onboarding.

next_safe_action: Design the P6 multi-project contract before implementation. Replace fixed research-engine project/repository/scale-set/runner assumptions with a root-owned project registry; replace experiment-specific privileged workload-name gates with semantic resource/capability validation; design a trusted Git-driven reconciliation path so subsequent approved repository onboarding requires no routine human terminal. PADataset is the first second-project pilot and must onboard without controller/provisioner/runtime source changes.
notes: Created after research-engine Wave-1 proved the complete GitHub-to-Lambda path and final cleanup receipt. PADataset is the first real second-project acceptance test, not another special-case workload.
